In this it is to be considered that, long after the time of David, the gluttonous shepherds being rejected, he says he will raise up our Lord, who is of the stock of David, to gather the lambs and cherish them in his bosom, and himself to carry on his shoulder the young of the sheep, or the ewes with young; as we read in the Gospel that he carried back to the fold on his shoulders the sheep that had strayed and stayed behind from its accustomed flock (Luke 15).

Then he will raise up one shepherd — who says in the Gospel: I am the good shepherd —, his servant David — inasmuch as he deigned to take on the form of a servant; and 'David' means 'strong of hand' —; he himself will feed them.

You will readily understand, brothers, that it is a prophecy of Christ coming to people from the seed of David, if you realize the dates. This prophet Ezekiel lived in the time of the captivity, which resulted from the exile of the people to Babylonia. From the time of David to the time of the exile there are fourteen generations.

And the Lord will be to them for God — either the Son and the Father, or certainly the shepherd according to the flesh he assumed. But 'Lord' and 'God' according to: The 'Word' that was in the beginning with 'God' —. This David, when the cattle have advanced to being a rational animal, will no longer be called shepherd but prince in the midst of them — of whom it is written: In the midst of you stands he whom you do not know —.
Pay close attention, brothers. Note the unity of the godhead, and yet the distribution of persons, in case we should say that he who is the Father is the Son, or that he who is the Son is the Father.

And when the beasts have been driven out and the land reduced to a solitude, they will sleep secure from animals of this sort and will say: The Lord is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear? —; and he will set them, those who will sleep secure, round about his mountain or hill, and they will be a blessing; then he will give rain in its season, and there will be rains of blessing — which he promises in the blessings of Deuteronomy —.

Then he will make with them a covenant of peace — by no means of wars and discord, for: His place was made in peace, but of the peace of Christ: Which surpasses all understanding —, who says: My peace I give to you, my peace I leave to you; and he will make the most evil beasts cease from the land — more mildly: either the passions by which human souls are troubled, or the adverse powers by which they are assailed —, and those who dwell in the desert will sleep secure in the woods — for the Lord will lay bare the thickets of the forests, and in his temple all will speak glory.

What is "in the desert"? In solitude. What is in solitude? Inside, in the conscience. It is a solitude indeed, because not only do no other human beings cross it, they do not even see it. Let us dwell there in hope, because we are not yet there in fact. After all, everything we have outside chops and changes with the storms and trials of the world. The desert is inside; that is where we should interrogate our faith.

There is also, of course, the bad sort of thunder shower, that knocks down the house built on sand, that it is a great thing even for the house founded on the rock to stand up against. That is the thunder shower of temptation, bent on devastation, not on irrigation, of the earth.

And the tree of life, he says, will give — of which it is written in Genesis —, and the tree of wisdom — of which it is said: It is a tree of life to all who take it up —: it will give its fruit when the earth too has given its fruit, or the trees of the regions, the very great multitude of the saints; and the earth will give its shoot: for Truth indeed has sprung from the earth; and they will be in their own land without fear, or in hope of peace, in the land of the living — the land of the meek, of which it is written: Blessed are the gentle, for they shall possess the land —, so that through the felicity of all things they may know that he himself is the Lord, when he has broken the chains or the iron ring of their yoke, by which they were pressed down as by a most heavy rule, and has rescued them from the hand of those ruling over them, or of those afflicting them with servitude: For each one is the slave of him by whom he is overcome.

[The fruitful trees are] in the plain, on level ground, not in rugged places, in a relatively easy life. Having things fairly easy in this life, with nothing steep or rugged, toilsome, difficult to cope with, this he calls the plain. Such is the life of many of the faithful in the church of God, who have their wives and husbands, children, families. They are like trees in the plain; they are not strong enough to climb anything steep or rugged. But only let them receive the shower; these trees too will give their fruit.

And they will by no means be a prey any longer to the demonic nations, nor will the beasts of the earth, of which we have spoken, devour them, but they will dwell confidently without any terror, according to the exposition above.

And I will raise up for them, he says, a renowned shoot (or a planting of peace) — which speaks in the Gospel: I am the true vine —, and they will no longer be diminished by famine in the land — so the famine is in earthly things; but the famine of hearing the word of God, which, under the good shepherd, and the renowned shoot, celebrated in the speech of all, and the planting of peace, will by no means be in the land —, nor will they be subject any longer to the reproaches of the nations — so that they say: Where is the Lord their God? —; and after all these things they will know, not only that he himself is the Lord — which he had also said above —, but, with an addition, that the Lord of all is properly their God, with them — who says in the Gospel to the apostles: Behold, I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the age —; and when he himself is the Lord their God, then they too will be his people: not just anyone, but those who have deserved to be called the house of Israel.
The church has been raised up to such a pinnacle in the name of Christ that all who curse are now put to shame and dare not curse anymore.

And lest we should think that all that has been said pertains to shepherds and sheep and he-goats and rams, he solves the riddle, or rather the μεταφορὰν, and sets it down more plainly: But you, my sheep, and the sheep of my pasture, are men; the whole discourse, therefore, is about men, to whom he says: I the Lord your God, says the Lord God.

O how blessed we are with such a possession and such a possessor! Because as well as him possessing us, we also possess him. He possesses us in order to tend us, and we possess him in order to tend him. But we tend him with worship as God, he tends us with cultivation as a field.
35: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, set (or turn) your face against Mount Seir, and you shall prophesy concerning it (or to it), and you shall say to it: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, Mount Seir; and I will stretch out my hand over you, and I will make you desolate and deserted. I will demolish your cities (or in your cities I will make a waste), and you shall be deserted, and you shall know that I am the Lord. Because you have been a perpetual enemy, and have shut up the sons of Israel into the hands of the sword (or and have laid siege to the house of Israel deceitfully in the hand of the sword) in the time of their affliction, in the time of the final iniquity; therefore, as I live, says the Lord God, I will hand you over to blood (or since you have sinned in blood), and blood pursues you, and since you have hated blood, blood pursues you. And I will make Mount Seir desolate and deserted, and I will take away from it him who goes and him who returns (or men and beasts), and I will fill its mountains with its slain (or wounded) in your hills, and in your valleys and torrents those slain by the sword shall fall. I will hand you over to everlasting wastes, and your cities shall not be inhabited, and you all shall know (or you shall know) that I am the Lord. Because you have said: Two nations and two lands (or regions) shall be mine, and I will possess them as an inheritance, though the Lord was there; therefore, as I live, says the Lord God, I will act according to your anger (or enmity), and according to your zeal which you showed, holding them in hatred, and I will be made known to you when I have judged you; and you shall know that I am the Lord. I have heard all your reproaches (or the voice of your blasphemies) which you have spoken (or that you have spoken) concerning the mountains of Israel: Deserted, they have been given to us to devour. And you rose up against me with your mouth (or you spoke boastfully against me with your mouth), and you have prayed against me (or you have shouted against me) your words; I have heard. Thus says the Lord God: While the whole earth rejoices, I will reduce you to a waste; as you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel because it was laid waste, so will I do to you: you shall be laid waste (or deserted), Mount Seir, and all Edom, and they shall know that I am the Lord. (But what is added in the Seventy, And they shall be consumed, is not found in the Hebrew.) If the word of God were always in the prophets and had a constant lodging in their breast, Ezekiel would never so often set down: 'And the word of the Lord came to me, saying'; but it was because, on account of human frailty and the necessities of this life, it at times withdrew from them; therefore John the Baptist says: He who sent me to baptize, he said to me: He on whom you see the Holy Spirit descending in the form of a dove and remaining in him, he it is — for what is added, And remaining in him, would never be something proper to Christ, unless it sometimes withdrew from others —; besides, God also says to Moses: I will take away from the spirit that is in you — which he certainly would not have had unless it had descended to him from the Lord —.

Now the whole prophecy of this chapter is against Mount Seir — namely of the sons of Esau and Edom, who in Greek and in our language are called Idumaeans [Edomites], because, in the time of need and distress, when Judah was being captured by the Babylonians, they insulted them, and, the people of the Jews having been cast out, they thought the land had been handed over to them to possess, and not only did they not take in his own sons, namely those of Jacob his brother, but they persecuted them and shut them up into the hands of the sword; whence Symmachus translated it more plainly: You have hated your blood, and blood pursues you —. It is prophesied, moreover, that he too is to be captured and reduced to everlasting wastes, and is to learn by the outcome of events that God is judge, because he said: Two nations and two regions are mine — either of the Edomites and the Jews, or surely of Judah and Israel, that is, of the two and the ten tribes —. And you spoke concerning the mountains of Israel, saying: Deserted, they have been given to us to devour, not considering that this blasphemy recoiled against God; hence there follows: While the whole earth rejoices, I will reduce you to a waste; and the sense is: 'When the whole land of Judea has recovered its former state, you will remain in an everlasting waste' — and what is added next: As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel because it was laid waste, so will I do to you, is not found in the Seventy, but has been added under asterisks from the edition of Theodotion —. But the whole wrath of God against Mount Seir tends to this end: that when it has been laid waste, both it and all Edom may know that he is the Lord. These things I would say according to the history, and hastily, the sense rather than the words; I shall pass to the ἀναγωγὴν [anagogy, the higher sense], and, for the sake of brevity, touch briefly on a few points.

Set, he says, (or turn) your face against Mount Seir; and he says 'turn' significantly: from one prophecy to another prophecy; and 'face': not of the body but of the mind — of which the Apostle also speaks: But we all, with unveiled face beholding the glory of the Lord —; and Mount 'Seir', which means 'shaggy' and 'hairy', is to be taken as the opposing power that presided over the nation of the sons of Esau and had raised itself up against the people of 'Iuda' [Judah], that is, of 'confession' and of the true faith — but if a prudent reader objects, how in this place 'Seir', that is, 'shaggy' and 'hairy', is understood in a bad sense when Elijah too was called a hairy man, I shall answer briefly: it is written of Esau that he was red and shaggy like a hide, but of Elijah only that he was a hairy man; in Esau, who, bloodthirsty and bloodstained, is compared to a shaggy hide, it is a sign of mortal works and of death itself; in Elijah, an increase of manliness, for which reason both his dwelling in the wilderness and the austerity of his way of life showed him to be not only a man but a most valiant man; moreover Jacob, who had supplanted Esau and received his birthright, because he dwelt simply at home and was not a hunter like the giant Nimrod, is for that reason called smooth and sleek —.

Let us see, then, what God commands to be said to the mountain, or against Mount Seir: 'Behold, I am against you, Mount Seir: I will not send angels, nor will I use other ministers, but I myself will come to you; and I will stretch out my hand over you, so as to take on the bearing of one who strikes, and I will make you desolate and deserted, so that you, who were wickedly inhabited and had very many companions in your impiety, to such a degree that you even built cities and claimed for yourself a dominion of your own, now, made desolate with your cities — which Jeremiah too is commanded to destroy and to dig up, so that he may build good cities in their place —, may profit in this, that you may know that I am the Lord, whom before you were laid waste you could not know'.

Now the whole cause of the sin is this: that he was a perpetual enemy; hence the psalm also says: Be angry and do not sin, so that we may quickly be reconciled with our enemies and exchange hatreds for love; but Mount Seir is not such, which, on top of its perpetual enmities, shut up, or besieged, the sons of Israel by guile in the hand of the sword; from which we understand that whoever has seized the sword against the sons of God and has done anything deceitfully and has besieged them has Mount Seir in the hand of the sword in the time of the final iniquity: when the days are most evil, and: The world is set in the evil one, and: Because iniquity is multiplied, the love of many grows cold.

There is, moreover, another sin of Mount Seir, so that, since it hated the blood of the righteous, which it longed to see poured out one by one in persecution after persecution, it suffers persecution from that very blood — whence also under the altar the souls of the saints keep crying out and beg the Lord for vengeance for their blood —.

And those who go and those who return are taken away from Mount Seir, that is, every inhabitant, or the men and beasts that are saved in the Church — of whom it is written: Men and beasts you will save, O Lord —; both of which are destroyed in Mount Seir, so that both those who seem to have some reason and those who are content with simple faith perish at God's command.

And its mountains are filled with the wounded and the slain; and not only the mountains, which have reached the summit of impiety, but the hills too, that is, the lesser disciples of Mount Seir, and the valleys, which are sunk into the depths, or the torrents, which have muddy waters, gathered from here and there and coming from pride, or, according to the Seventy, the plains, which lie midway between hills and valleys: all these, slain, shall fall by the sword of the Lord and of his outstretched and striking hand, so that they may be reduced to everlasting wastes; and if there were any cities, that is, gatherings of an evil habitation, they too are to perish and cease to hold agreement in the bad sense, and their tongues are to be divided, so that they cannot build a tower of blasphemy against God; and, reduced to a waste and a desert, let them know that he is the Lord.

Nor was it enough for Mount Seir to have said so much and done so much, as the preceding discourse has related, but this too it spoke in its pride: 'Two nations and two lands (or regions) are mine: namely, both Edom and Judea, both heretics and churchmen, I shall possess alike'. 'And this', he says, 'you said while the Lord was there, who presided over his people'.

Therefore the Lord swears and says: 'As I live, says the Lord God, according to your anger with which you raged against the people of God, and your zeal with which you persecuted the household of Christ, holding in hatred those whom you longed to possess, when I have struck you and judged you, then I will be made known to you. And you shall know that I learned of your reproaches and blasphemies not through another's report, but that I myself heard what you spoke against the mountains of Israel, saying: Deserted, they have been given to us to devour, the mountains of Israel' — we ought to understand Moses, the prophets, the apostles, whom the heretics and the prince of heretics, the devil, think have been handed over to them to devour, when either rarely anyone or no one is found in the Church who can fight for the mountains of the Lord and ward off their mangling with his voice —.

'And you rose up', he says, 'against me with your mouth, or you spoke boastfully, not, as you think, against the mountains, but through them against me; and you prayed, or cried out, against me; for all your prayers, O Mount Seir and companions of Mount Seir — of whom it was said above: I will fill its mountains and hills and valleys and plains (or torrents) —, were against me: not at all prayers and petitions, as you think, to God, but a clamor of shouting and blasphemy'.

Hence the Lord also threatens and says: 'As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel when by your persecutions it was laid waste and torn and scattered through the whole world, so will I do to you: for while the whole land of the living and the land of the saints rejoices, and all are turned to the service of God, you shall be laid waste, shaggy mountain, hairy mountain, and all Edom — namely, earthly works given over to gore and blood —, so that then you may know that I am the Lord, who have said elsewhere: I am the Lord your God'.
36: These things we have said παραφραστικῶς [by way of paraphrase], in the Jewish manner: things which they expect in the reign of a thousand years, when they assert that the city of Jerusalem is to be built, and the temple which is described at the end of this volume, and the happiness of all things; and some of them think that these things were fulfilled under Zerubbabel — but how can what is said stand: And I will make you to be inhabited as from the beginning, and I will endow you with greater goods than you had from the beginning? For under Zerubbabel, Ezra and Nehemiah few of the people were brought back, and they themselves, obeying the Medes and Persians and thereafter the Macedonians and Egyptians and Romans, served the kings of various nations up to Titus and Vespasian, and serve them to this day, so that what is said at the end of the prophecy cannot stand at all: And the reproach of the peoples thou shalt by no means bear, and thou shalt no more lose thy nation —; and since it would be a long matter to speak now, in a brief explanation, against the Jewish dogma and against a blessedness that serves the belly and gullet of the Jews, who desire all earthly things and say: Let us eat and drink — of whom the Apostle also speaks: Food is for the belly and the belly for foods; but God will destroy both it and them —, let us now pass to the spiritual understanding, according to which we also interpreted the last parts of Isaiah. For we do not, according to the Jewish fables which they call δευτερώσεις [deuteroses, secondary traditions], expect a jeweled and golden Jerusalem from heaven, nor are we going to suffer again the injury of circumcision, nor to offer victims of bulls and rams, nor shall we sleep in the idleness of the sabbath — which many of our own also promise, and especially the book of Tertullian entitled 'On the Hope of the Faithful' and the seventh volume of Lactantius' 'Institutes', and the frequent 'Expositions' of Victorinus, bishop of Poetovio, and recently our Severus in the dialogue to which he gave the name 'Gallus', and, to name the Greeks and join the first and the last, Irenaeus and Apollinaris —.

We, therefore, say that the mountains of Israel are the prophets and apostles, who hear the word of God and whom the devil, the enemy, insulted, saying: 'Aha, the mountains once lofty — of which it is written: Mountains are round about it, and the Lord is round about his people — have been given to me as a possession, when through the straits of persecution they were made desolate and trampled down round about, and made an inheritance for the rest of the nations, and blasphemed by all'.

But you, son of man, prophesy over the mountains of Israel, and you shall say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord God: Because the enemy has said of you: Aha, the everlasting heights (or solitudes) have been given to us as a possession; therefore prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord God: Because you have been made desolate and trampled down round about (or Because you have been scattered by those who are round about you), and made an inheritance (or a possession) for the rest of the nations, and you have come up upon the lip of the tongue and become a reproach to the peoples (or nations); therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord God: Thus says the Lord God to the mountains and the hills, to the torrents and the valleys and the deserts, to the ruined walls (or the things scattered) and the forsaken cities, which have been depopulated and derided (or trampled down) by the rest of the nations round about. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Since in the fire of my zeal I have spoken concerning the rest of the nations, and concerning all Edom, who have given my land to themselves as an inheritance with joy and with the whole heart and from the soul, and have cast it out in order to lay it waste (or with joy, despising souls, in order to overthrow them in devastation), therefore prophesy over the land of Israel, and you shall say to the mountains and the hills, to the ridges and the valleys: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I have spoken in my zeal and in my fury, because you have borne the confusion (or the reproaches) of the nations; therefore thus says the Lord God (or Adonai the Lord): I have lifted up (or I will lift up) my hand, so that the nations which are round about you shall themselves bear their confusion (or ignominy); but you, mountains of Israel, shall put forth your branches (or your grapes), and bear your fruit for my people Israel, for it is near that it should come. For behold, I am toward you, and I will turn to you (or I will look upon you), and you shall be plowed and shall receive seed; and I will multiply men upon you, and the whole house of Israel, and the cities shall be inhabited and the ruined places shall be restored (or what is deserted shall be built). And I will fill you with men and with beasts, and they shall be multiplied and shall increase; and I will make you to be inhabited as from the beginning, and I will endow you with greater goods than you had from the beginning, and you shall know that I am the Lord. And I will bring (or I will beget) upon you men, my people Israel, and they shall possess thee by inheritance (or you), and thou shalt be (or you shall be) a possession for them, and thou shalt not add any more to be without them (or and you shall not add any more that they should make you without children). Thus says the Lord God: Because they have said of you (or to thee): Thou art a devourer of men, and one who strangles thy nation; therefore thou shalt no more eat men, and thou shalt no longer kill thy nation, says the Lord God. Nor will I any more cause the confusion (or ignominy) of the nations to be heard in thee (or in you), and the reproaches of the peoples thou shalt by no means bear (or you shall bear), and thou shalt no more lose thy nation (or thy nation shall no longer be without children), says the Lord God. Above, the prophet's face is set, or turned, against Mount Seir; here the son of man speaks to the mountains, or over the mountains, of Israel, which are commanded to hear the word of God; and, to put off the tropology for a little, this in brief is the sense of the whole prophecy to the mountains of Israel: 'Because the enemy, that is, Mount Seir, insulted you, and thought that he himself would possess you forever, and that the heights, once the Lord's and now deserted, had passed to him as an inheritance, and not only said so but also possessed you for some time, to such a degree that he spoke proudly against you and you were a reproach to all the nations, therefore thus says the Lord God, not only to Mount Seir, but also to its mountains and hills, torrents, valleys and deserts and wasted places and forsaken cities: that in the fire of his zeal he has spoken, against all the nations indeed, but especially against Edom, which with the other' he says 'nations held my land as a possession, and possessed it with joy, and possessed it with the whole heart, so as to cast the inhabitants out of it and lay the land waste.

Therefore the Lord speaks to the mountains trampled down and made desolate, and not only to the mountains but also to those lower down, set at their several degrees in the land of Judea, that is, on the mountain of the Church — of which it is written: A city set upon a mountain cannot be hidden —, and to the hills and torrents, whose faith is increased by the winter of persecutions and the storm of affliction, to the valleys also, those who have been brought low in humility, and to the deserted churches, and to the ruined walls, and to the meeting places of the churches forsaken throughout the whole world — such was the persecution throughout the whole world under Diocletian and Maximian, through which the churches were proscribed and laid waste, when all the nations of the Gentiles and of the heretics round about derided the Church —: that he has spoken in the fire of the zeal of his fury; and particularly against Edom, which by earthly works wanted everyone to lay aside the image of the heavenly and bear the image of the earthly: for they gave the land of God to themselves as an inheritance, and with the whole heart and from the soul they persecuted the Church of the Lord, and cast it out of its seats, and laid it waste.

For hence it is that under the figure of the Idumaeans, who allowed themselves to be vanquished by their own prosperity, those who rejoice in the successes of this world are rebuked, when it is said, "They have given my land to themselves for an inheritance with joy, and with their whole heart and mind." In which words it is to be observed, that they are smitten with severe rebuke, not merely because they rejoice, but because they rejoice with their whole heart and mind.

Therefore speak,' he says, 'O prophet, over the land of Israel, and you shall say to the mountains and hills and ridges — for which the Seventy translated νάπας [glens], which we understand as 'places' that are 'wooded' —, and to the valleys: Thus says the Lord God: In my zeal and in my fury I will stand forth as the avenger of your reproach; and I will lift up my hand, so that the nations which are round about you may bear their ignominy and confusion; but you, O mountains of Israel, shall sprout according to your former state, and put forth shoots and branches — or, according to the Seventy, bear grapes —, with which my people Israel may be filled; and do not think that this will come after a long time: it is near, the time is at hand and will come.

But what did it profit the nations, what did it help the nations of heretics to have insulted the land of the Lord, when the Lord speaks to it, and has spoken in his zeal and in his fury to its mountains and hills and ridges, or wooded places, which were green with the loveliness of paradise, and to the hills, of which we spoke above, and lifts up his hand, on account of the reproach of the nations, against the adversaries who persecuted the Church, so that they bear their confusion and ignominy?: then, when the persecutors have been slain and peace has been restored to the Church, the mountains of Israel, namely the apostles and apostolic men, will make their trees sprout and stretch out their branches, and will bring grapes to be trodden in the winepress of the Lord, from which the new wine flows that inebriates the peoples of believers, and the wine is pressed out that gladdens the heart of man, so that all the fruit of the mountains, from which is made the bread descending from heaven, may be eaten by the people of God, Israel.

And lest perhaps we despair in persecutions, it is added: It is near — the time — that it should come — for coming indeed he will come and will not delay —; hence he promises his coming to the mountains and to those who have endured in tribulations, and promises that, after the heat of persecution, the land formerly stripped may be worked by the plowshare of Christ, and receive every seed of the virtues, from which men may be born and multiplied, and the whole house of Israel.
I will strengthen the people's hope, and I will make steadfast their expectation of good things to come, and they will return and enjoy those fruits that are produced by you.

And lest this seem difficult to you, I myself will come to you, and I who had withdrawn from you will turn to you, so that you may recover your former cultivation and all things may be filled with seed, so that there may be many men in you, and the cities which had formerly been destroyed may be inhabited. And not only will I multiply men, but the beasts too shall likewise be multiplied and shall increase; and I will make you to be inhabited as from the beginning, when, under the leadership of Moses, two and a half tribes received their possession beyond the Jordan, and, under Joshua the son of Nun, the other nine and a half tribes possessed the land of Judea; and I will endow you with goods much greater than you were from the beginning, before you experienced the various captivities; and when I have done this for you, then you will know that I am the Lord.

And when the cities, that is, the churches of believers, have been inhabited by the returning crowds, then not only the men who will be strong in the knowledge of the Scriptures, but also the beasts, all the simple among the believers, will be multiplied and grow up; and the churches will be inhabited as from the beginning, that is, before there was persecution, and will flourish with greater goods than they had from the beginning, crowned with the victories of the martyrs. And then they will know that he is the Lord who restores his people to its former state, so that it may possess the churches and itself be the inheritance of the churches, and no longer be without the children whom it had lost in persecution.

Since then God blesses this people, and calls them Israel, and declares them to be His inheritance, how is it that you repent not of the deception you practise on yourselves, as if you alone were the Israel, and of execrating the people whom God has blessed? For when He speaks to Jerusalem and its environs, He thus added: 'And I will beget men upon you, even my people Israel; and they shall inherit you, and you shall be a possession for them; and you shall be no longer bereaved of them.'
And you shall be filled,' he says, 'O land of Israel, with my people, who will hold you as an inheritance, and you shall be a possession for them, and you shall not add any more to be without sons.

But when your inhabitant has been multiplied, O mountains of Israel, then your enemies will by no means say against you that you devour men and that your possession is without children; but on the contrary you will multiply men, and your posterity will bring forth a most abundant offspring. Nor will you hear,' he says, 'any more, nor will you bear, the confusion of the nations; nor yet will you lose your nation so as ever to undergo captivity, since the Lord has spoken'.

Hence the prophet is commanded to speak to the land of the meek and the land of the living, or to the mountains of Israel, and to say: 'You shall no longer suffer the reproach of the persecutors, nor will they insult your slaughtered people as sheep for the slaughter; for when peace has been restored, all reproaches will cease, nor will you bear confusion and ignominy among the various nations round about, but you will have your nation and your people, because the truth of the promise has been confirmed, since the Lord has spoken'.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, the house of Israel have dwelt (or has dwelt) in their land, and they defiled it in their ways and in their pursuits (or idols); like the uncleanness of a menstruous woman their way has become before me. And I poured out my indignation (or my fury) upon them, for the blood which they shed upon the land; with their idols they defiled it. And I scattered them among the nations, and they were winnowed (or I winnowed them) into the lands (or into the regions); according to their ways and their devices (or sins) I judged them. And they went in to the nations to which they entered, and they defiled my holy name, when it was said of them: This is the people of the Lord, and they have gone out of his land. And I spared my holy name (or I spared them for the sake of my holy name), which the house of Israel had defiled among the nations to which they went in. Therefore you shall say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Not for your sake will I act, house of Israel, but for the sake of my holy name, which you defiled among the nations to which you entered; and I will sanctify my great name, which has been defiled among the nations, which you defiled in the midst of them, so that they may know that I am the Lord, says the Lord of hosts, when I shall have been sanctified in you before them. For I will take you from the nations, and gather you from all the lands, and bring you into your own land; and I will pour out (or sprinkle) clean water upon you, and you shall be cleansed from all your defilements, and from all your idols I will cleanse you. And I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put in your midst (or I will give you), and I will take away the heart of stone out of your flesh, and give you a heart of flesh; and my spirit I will put in your midst (or I will give you), and I will cause you to walk in my precepts (or in my justifications), and to keep my judgments and to work (or do) them. And you shall dwell in the land which I gave to your fathers, and you shall be to me for a people and I will be to you for a God. And I will save you from all your defilements (or uncleannesses), and I will call the fruit and multiply it, and I will not lay (or give) famine upon you. And I will multiply the fruit of the tree and the produce of the field, so that you may no longer bear the reproach of famine among the nations. And you shall remember your most evil ways, and your pursuits that were not good, and your iniquities and your crimes shall displease you. Not for your sake will I act, says the Lord God; let it be known to you: be confounded and blush for your ways, house of Israel. Thus says the Lord God: On the day when I shall have cleansed you from all your iniquities, and caused the cities to be inhabited and restored the ruined places, and the deserted land shall have been tilled which once was desolate in the eyes of every traveler, they will say: That untilled land (or deserted) has become like a garden of pleasure, and the cities deserted and forsaken and undermined have sat fortified. And the nations which shall have been left round about you will know that I the Lord have built what was scattered and planted what was untilled; that I the Lord have spoken and have done it. Thus says the Lord God: Yet in this will the house of Israel find me (or I will be sought by the house of Israel), that I may do it for them: I will multiply them like a flock of men (or like sheep, men), like a holy flock (or like holy sheep), like the flock (or sheep) of Jerusalem in her solemn feasts: so shall the deserted cities also be full of flocks (or sheep) of men, and they shall know that I am the Lord. What is said is clear, and the whole sense concerning the mountains of Israel, which had formerly been deserted and were afterwards restored, is now set out more plainly; and God gives the reasons why he handed the people of Israel over to captivity, and on account of his clemency promises that he will lead them back into the land of Judea, and bestow far more than he had taken away — which some of the Jews refer to the times of Zerubbabel, when, as Cyrus king of the Persians relaxed their captivity, very many from the tribe of Judah and Benjamin were brought back into Judea; but others refer it to the reign of a thousand years, when under the Christ, who they think is yet to come, both the city of Jerusalem is to be built up and the temple to be built, of which we shall speak in the last part of this prophecy —. And meanwhile, to leave behind Jewish fables and endless genealogies, let us, according to our custom, briefly run through the περικοπὴν [section] of this chapter, and set out what seems right to us according to the ecclesiastical understanding.

Whoever is of the house of Israel and sees the peace of Christ, which surpasses all understanding, dwells in his own land, the Church, or in the lodging of the flesh which has been handed over to him by God; but if he defiles either land in his most evil ways and is compared to the uncleanness of a menstruous woman, God pours out his indignation upon him, for the blood, whether his own or that of those whom he has scandalized and has shed upon the land, and for the perverse thoughts with which he defiled it.

The house of Israel, that is, the people of the Jews, once dwelt in its own land, that is, in the land of Judea, when it was led out of Egypt; but they defiled it in their ways and in their pursuits, or idols; and they became so polluted that they were compared to the uncleanness of a menstruous woman.

On which account God pours out his indignation upon them for the blood of the prophets and the righteous which they shed upon the land — as the Savior says in the Gospel: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those who have been sent to you, and again: Amen, amen I say to you: the blood which has been shed shall be required of this generation, from the blood of Abel the righteous up to the blood of Zechariah the son of Barachiah, which they shed between the altar and the temple —; and not only did they shed blood, but they also defiled the land with their crimes; for which reason he scattered them, whether under the Babylonian captivity or under the Roman, when they truly shed the blood of Christ; and they were winnowed into the lands as chaff is winnowed, and judged according to their ways and their most evil inventions, so that among the nations too, to which they had been led captive, they defiled the holy name of God, because all the nations said in mockery: 'Behold, this is the people of God, which boasted that it properly knew the worship of God'.

Then he will be scattered among the nations so as to be made equal to the unbelieving nations, and he will be winnowed on the earth like chaff so as to be separated from the grain of the Church, and he will be judged according to his ways; and if not even so does he perceive his sin, but defiles his holy name, all among whom he dwells will say: 'Behold the people of God, behold one who went out of his land, or rather was cast out'.

If we pursue virtue, let us seek before all to gain for ourselves the approval that comes from God alone, and let us take no account of human praise. If we are lax, we should be afraid and humble our thinking with the thought of that judgment that cannot be bribed. Let us tremble at the approach of that dread day and the thought that our actions provoke blasphemy against God.

All these sacraments may be possessed by the evil person; but to have charity and be an evil person is not possible. This therefore is the peculiar gift of the Spirit: he is the one and only fountain. To drink of it, God's Spirit calls you: God's Spirit calls you to drink of himself.

'When I had seen this,' he says, 'not for their sake but for the sake of my holy name — for I am the Creator of all — I spared them; and I sanctified them and restored them to their former glory, so that upon those who believed and were converted from error I poured out the clean water of saving baptism, and cleansed them from their abominations and from all the errors with which they had been taken up; and I gave them a new heart, that they might believe in the Son of God, and a new spirit' — of which David speaks: Create a clean heart in me, O God, and renew a right spirit in my inward parts —.

In another passage, also, by the same prophet, God, in the clearest language, shows us that it is not owing to any good merits on the part of men, but for His own name's sake, that He does these things. This is His language: "This I do, O house of Israel, but for mine holy name's sake, which ye have profaned among the heathen, whither ye went. And I will sanctify my great name, which was profaned among the heathen, which ye have profaned in the midst of them; and the heathen shall know that I am the Lord, saith the Lord God, when I shall be sanctified in you before their eyes. For I will take you from among the heathen, and gather you out of all countries, and will bring you into your own land. Then will I sprinkle you with clean water, and ye shall be clean: from all your own filthiness, and from all your idols will I cleanse you. A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you; and the stony heart shall be taken away out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh. And I will put my Spirit within you, and will cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them." Now who is so blind as not to see, and who so stone-like as not to feel, that this grace is not given according to the merits of a good will, when the Lord declares and testifies, "It is I, O house of Israel, who do this, but for my holy name's sake"? Now why did He say "It is I that do it, but for my holy name's sake," were it not that they should not think that it was owing to their own good merits that these things were happening, as the Pelagians hesitate not unblushingly to say? But there were not only no good merits of theirs, but the Lord shows that evil ones actually preceded; for He says, "But for my holy name's sake, which ye have profaned among the heathen." Who can fail to observe how dreadful is the evil of profaning the Lord's own holy name? And yet, for the sake of this very name of mine, says He, which ye have profaned, I, even I, will make you good, but not for your own sakes; and, as He adds, "I will sanctify my great name, which was profaned among the heathen, which ye have profaned in the midst of them." He says that He sanctifies His name, which He had already declared to be holy. Therefore, this is just what we pray for in the Lord's Prayer—"Hallowed be Thy name." We ask for the hallowing among men of that which is in itself undoubtedly always holy. Then it follows, "And the heathen shall know that I am the Lord, saith the Lord God, when I shall be sanctified in you." Although, then, He is Himself always holy, He is, nevertheless, sanctified in those on whom He bestows His grace, by taking from them that stony heart by which they profaned the name of the Lord.

God by his grace takes away the stony heart from unbelievers and forestalls merit in people of good will in such a way that their will is prepared by what goes before grace, but that grace is not given through some merit of human will.

Lest, however, it should be thought that men themselves in this matter do nothing by free will, it is said in the Psalm, "Harden not your hearts;" and in Ezekiel himself, "Cast away from you all your transgressions, which ye have impiously committed against me; and make you a new heart and a new spirit; and keep all my commandments. Then the fruit of the tree will be multiplied — that is, of wisdom, of which it is written: She is a tree of life to all who seek her — and the produce of the field — in the likeness of Jacob, whose smell was: Like the smell of a full field which the Lord has blessed —, and they will no longer bear the reproach of famine among the nations, which the unbelief of the Jews suffers even today; but, after they have attained blessedness, they will imitate the Apostle, who says: I am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the Church of God.

That penitents may have their due it is enough for them to feel shame instead of all other punishment.

And they will remember their most evil ways and their pursuits that were not good, by which they had offended God, and their iniquities and their crimes, by which they had formerly gone astray, will displease them.

Hence he also exhorts those who stray to be confounded and to blush for their ways, and to be restored to the cities of the Church, so that these may again be inhabited by them, and everything that had collapsed in them may be built up, and they may return to their former ceremonies, and the land once deserted, which had seemed desolate to the neighbors and strangers and to those passing through the conduct of this world, may return to its former state, and all may marvel and say: 'That untilled land, that deserted land in which all the virtues once perished, has now become like a garden of pleasure and the paradise of God'; and the cities once deserted, which did not have God as their guest and were forsaken by the Holy Spirit and undermined by unbelief, will be fortified by the faith of Christ, so that all round about may know that the Lord has built up the scattered souls, and planted in them and sown together the trees of all the virtues, and that he who promised by word has himself made it good in deed.

Now the Lord will bestow all these things, not for the sake of those who perished by their own error, but for the sake of his holy name; hence he challenges the house of Israel to be confounded and to blush for its former vices, and to understand its Creator.

But after he has cleansed the people of believers from among the Jews from their iniquities, and caused the cities of the Church to be inhabited, and restored the ruined places which had fallen in the synagogues, and the land of confession has been tilled with the ceremonies of God, which once seemed desolate to all the saints who pass by the works of earthly conduct, then all will say: 'How is it that the land of Judea, which had once been untilled, now has the likeness of the paradise of God, and the cities of Judea, which had been deserted and forsaken and undermined by their own unbelief, are now raised up and fortified in the confession and the name of the Lord Savior?'; so that every creature, and the multitudes of angels that encircle the land of Israel, may know that the Lord has built the scattered cities and planted the untilled regions, and has fulfilled in deed what he promised through the prophets.

Nor will he be content with this gift of his liberality toward the people he has saved, but he will bestow far greater things: for he will be found by the house of Israel, he who had been sought for a long time and not found; and, after it has found him, he will multiply them like sheep, not sheep of brute animals but sheep of men — who are full of reason and confession —, like holy sheep and the flock of Jerusalem — in which properly is the worship of God and the vision of peace —, in her solemn feasts — when we eat the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth, and feed on the flesh of the Lamb and are given his blood to drink, and in the seven weeks and in the tabernacles of this age, of the Lord, of the Lord, celebrate the feasts —, so that the cities, once deserted, may become full of flocks of men, and by this means they may know that he is the Lord who has bestowed all things. Let it suffice to have said these things briefly according to the truth of the history, or rather according to the faith of the prophecy: how the people of Israel is restored to its unimpaired state, and the remnant of the people of the Jews, as the Apostle Paul teaches, is saved in the apostles and in all who from the Jews believed in the beginning and to this day return to the Church; now the sense of the tropology must be opened with the same brevity.

And again the prophetic word exhorts the penitent that, even when they have returned into the churches, they should always seek the Lord and find him, so that the flocks of the Lord may be multiplied by the crowds of those returning, not flocks of beasts and brute animals, but flocks of men who are full of faith and reason, holy flocks, flocks of the city of Jerusalem, in all the solemn feasts which they have received by the clemency of God, so that, after a multitude of such flocks has filled the cities of the Lord, then all may know that he is the Lord.

And also through the Prophet Ezekiel, the Resurrection of the dead was manifestly shown, when God brought him forth to the valley and showed him many bones, and made him pass by them round about them, and said to him:—Son of Man, will these bones live? And Ezekiel said to Him:—Thou knowest, O Lord of lords. And the Lord said to him:—Prophesy, O Son Man, over these bones; prophesy and say to the dry bones, Hear the word of the Lord of lords. And when he had caused them to hear those words, there was a shaking and a noise, and the bones were gathered together, even those that were crushed into pieces and broken. The hope of resurrection is the root of every kind of good work, for the expectation of reward braces the soul to productive toil. And whereas every worker is ready to sustain his toil if he can look forward to being repaid for his labors, where toil has no recompense the soul is soon discouraged and the body flags with it. A soldier who expects his share of the spoils is ready for war. But no one is prepared to die serving a king so undiscerning that he does not provide rewards for labors. In the same way, any soul that believes in resurrection takes care for itself, as is right, but any soul that disbelieves the resurrection abandons itself to destruction. A person who believes that the body survives to rise again is careful of this garment and does not soil it by fornicating. But a person who does not believe in the resurrection gives himself up to fornication, abusing his own body as if it were nothing to him. A mighty message and teaching of the holy Catholic church is belief about the resurrection of the dead; mighty and most indispensable. While many deny it, the truth claims credence for it. Greeks deny it, Samaritans disbelieve, while heretics tear away the half. Truth never appears but in one shape, while contradiction assumes a hundred.

For instance, Ezekiel leaps in the spirit of prophecy over all the intervening time, with its vast duration; he stands, by his powers of foresight, in the actual moment of the Resurrection, and, as if he had really gazed on what is still to come, brings it in his description before our eyes. He saw a mighty plain, unfolded to an endless distance before him, and vast heaps of bones upon it flung at random, some this way, some that; and then under an impulse from God these bones began to move and group themselves with their fellows that they once owned, and adhere to the familiar sockets, and then clothe themselves with muscle, flesh, and skin (which was the process called "decorating" in the poetry of the Psalms); a Spirit in fact was giving life and movement to everything that lay there.

There were at all events many wonderful and great prophets among ourselves who spoke many things about the future, and they in no way used to bid those who asked them to dig up the bones of the departed. But those who interpret otherwise will put forward the following: it ought not to bring odium upon us that, by expounding this passage otherwise, we seem to deny the resurrection: for we know that we find in the holy Scriptures much stronger testimonies, and ones in which there is no doubt — such as that of Job: You will raise up my skin, which endures these things, and in Daniel: Many who sleep in the dust of the earth shall rise again, these to life eternal, and these to reproach and to eternal confusion, and in the Gospel: Do not fear those who kill the body and cannot kill the soul; but rather fear him who can destroy both soul and body in gehenna, and in the apostle Paul: Who will give life to your mortal bodies because of his spirit dwelling in you, and many others —; from which it is clear that we do not deny the resurrection, but contend that these things were not written of the resurrection and that, through the parable of the resurrection, it is the restoration of Israel that is prophesied, which at that time was captive in Babylon. Nor shall we at once give an occasion to heretics if we deny that these things are to be understood of the common resurrection: for the likeness of the resurrection would never be set forth to signify the restoration of the Israelite people, unless the resurrection itself stood firm and were believed to be in the future — since no one confirms uncertain things from things that do not exist —; and our whole assertion tends to this: that, just as it seems unbelievable that a future resurrection should be promised to dry bones worn away by great age, and yet what is promised will be, so also the restoration of the people of Israel, which was led into captivity and scattered over the whole world, seems indeed incredible to those who do not know the power of God, but yet it will be: 'For I' he says 'the Lord have spoken and will do it, as I have promised'. But the Jews affirm that all these things were fulfilled either under Zerubbabel, as I said before, when a great commotion took place and the kingdom of the Chaldeans was transferred to the Medes and Persians, or at the presence of their Christ, who they think is yet to come. And he said to me: Son of man, do you think these bones will live? And I said: Lord God, you know. And he said to me: Prophesy concerning these bones, and you shall say to them: Dry bones, hear the word of the Lord; thus says the Lord God to these bones: Behold, I will send spirit into you and you shall live, and I will put sinews upon you and make flesh grow up upon you, and I will stretch skin over you, and I will give you spirit, and you shall live, and you shall know that I am the Lord. And I prophesied as he had commanded me. And there was a sound, as I prophesied, and behold, a commotion; and the bones drew near, bones to bones, each one to its joint. And I looked, and behold, sinews and flesh came up upon them, and skin was stretched over them from above, and they did not have spirit. And he said to me: Prophesy to the spirit; prophesy, son of man, and you shall say to the spirit: Thus says the Lord God: Come from the four winds, O spirit, and breathe upon these slain, and let them come to life again. And I prophesied as he had commanded me, and the spirit entered into them; and they lived, and they stood upon their feet, an army great beyond measure, exceedingly. And he said to me: Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel; they say: Our bones have dried up and our hope has perished, and we are cut off. Therefore prophesy and you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will open your tombs, and I will lead you out of your graves, my people, and I will bring you into the land of Israel; and you shall know that I am the Lord, when I have opened your graves and have led you out of your tombs, my people, and have put my spirit in you and you have lived, and I will make you rest upon your own soil, and you shall know that I am the Lord: I have spoken and I have done it, says the Lord God. (LXX: "And the hand of the Lord came upon me, and he led me out in the spirit of the Lord, and placed me in the midst of a plain, and this was full of the bones of men; and he led me around over them by a circuit round about: and behold, very many upon the face of the plain, and dry exceedingly. And he said to me: Son of man, will these bones live? And I said: Lord, Lord, you know these things. And he said to me: Son of man, prophesy over these bones, and you shall say to them: Dry bones, hear the word of the Lord; thus says the Lord God to these bones: Behold, I will bring upon you the spirit of life, and I will put sinews upon you and bring flesh upon you, and I will stretch hide over you, and I will give you my spirit, and you shall live, and you shall know that I am the Lord. And I prophesied as he commanded me. And there was a voice, when I was prophesying, and behold, a commotion; and the bones were drawing near, bones to bones, to its joint. And I looked, and behold, sinews and flesh were springing up upon them, and hides were coming up over them from above, and there was no spirit in them. And he said to me: Prophesy over the spirit, prophesy, son of man, and say to the spirit: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Come from the four spirits, O spirit, and breathe upon these dead, and let them live. And I prophesied as he had commanded me, and the spirit entered into them; and they lived, and stood on their feet, a congregation large, exceedingly, beyond measure. And the Lord spoke to me, saying: Son of man, these bones are all the house of Israel; they say: Our bones have become dry, our hope has perished, we have despaired. Therefore prophesy, and say to them: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I will open your memorials, and I will bring you back from your graves, my people, and I will bring you into the land of Israel; and you shall know that I am the Lord, when I have opened your graves so as to lead you out of your graves, my people, and I will give my spirit in you and you shall live, and I will place you upon your own land, and you shall know that I am the Lord: I have spoken and I will do it, says the Lord, the Lord.") The vision is a famous one, and celebrated in the reading of all the churches of Christ; and for this reason above all I have set down both editions in full, so that no calumny might be raised against us by the Hebrews if they differed even in some words — for they are accustomed to laugh at us and to raise their eyebrows, and with puffed-out cheeks to belch forth their knowledge of the Scriptures, if they have been able to point out in our codices, I will not say a discrepancy of sense — which, if there were one, is rightly censured — but a dissonance of words —. Those, then, who think that the word of God is about the resurrection — which is believed by all, both Jews and Christians — are accustomed to say this: The hand of the Lord came upon the prophet, that is, the Lord and Savior, through whom the Father wrought all things — All things indeed were made by him, and without him nothing was made that was made —. And he led me out, he says, in the spirit of the Lord: the hand of the Lord is understood; and he led him out in the spirit: not in the body but outside the body, and placed him, or set him down, in the midst of a plain which was full of human bones; nor did it allow him to rest, but made him go around all the bones, which were not covered with earth but lying upon the plain: and not only many, but very many and, because of the length of time, dry and exceedingly parched and having no moisture in them.
Again this is the spirit of contemplation; he did not see these bodies that were shown to him with his eyes, but he had them revealed to him by the Holy Spirit.
And when the divine word had asked him whether he thought these bones could live, he replied: 'Lord God, you know, you who have full knowledge of things to come'.

In minute detail the holy prophet Ezekiel teaches and describes how strength will be restored to our dry bones, feeling return and motion added; how, with the return of sinews, the whole structure of the human body will grow strong, and how the driest bones will be clothed with restored flesh and the openings of the veins and the streams of the blood will be concealed by a veil of skin drawn tautly over them. At the very words of the prophet, as we read, the crop of human bodies seems to rise up again to life, and one may see the wide expanses of the fields sprouting with a novel kind of growth.

Note how the prophet shows that there was hearing and movement in the bones before the Spirit of life was poured on them. For, above, both the dry bones are bidden to hear, as if they had the sense of hearing, and that on this each of them came to its own joint is pointed out by the words of the prophet.…Great is the lovingkindness of the Lord, that the prophet is taken as a witness of the future resurrection, that we, too, might see it with his eyes. For all could not be taken as witnesses, but in that one all we are witnesses, for neither does lying come on a holy person or error on so great a prophet.

And the Lord said to him: Prophesy concerning the bones (or over these bones), and you shall say to them: Dry bones, hear the word of the Lord. In this it is to be wondered at how he spoke to dry bones, which, before the sinews, flesh and skin and the life-giving spirit, could hear the word of God; and first bones are bound to other bones by the bonds of sinews, then they are filled with flesh, and over them, for beauty, skin is stretched to cover the unsightliness of the bare flesh, and then they receive the spirit which makes them live, so that, after they have lived, they may then know that he is the Lord.

There should … be certain bones of the inner person in which the bond of union and harmony of spiritual powers is collected. Just as the bones by their own firmness protect the tenderness of the flesh, so also in the church there are some who through their own constancy are able to carry the infirmities of the weak. And as the bones are joined to each other through articulations by sinews and fastenings that have grown on them, so also would be the bond of charity and peace, which achieves a certain natural junction and union of the spiritual bones in the church of God.

For the prophets have proclaimed two advents of His: the one, that which is already past, when He came as a dishonoured and suffering Man; but the second, when, according to prophecy, He shall come from heaven with glory, accompanied by His angelic host, when also He shall raise the bodies of all men who have lived, and shall clothe those of the worthy with immortality, and shall send those of the wicked, endued with eternal sensibility, into everlasting fire with the wicked devils. And that these things also have been foretold as yet to be, we will prove. By Ezekiel the prophet it was said: "Joint shall be joined to joint, and bone to bone, and flesh shall grow again; and every knee shall bow to the Lord, and every tongue shall confess Him." And in what kind of sensation and punishment the wicked are to be, hear from what was said in like manner with reference to this; it is as follows: "Their worm shall not rest, and their fire shall not be quenched;" and then shall they repent, when it profits them not.

After this was seen the sight which had been desired and prayed for by us all; feasts of dedication in the cities and consecrations of the newly built houses of prayer took place, bishops assembled, foreigners came together from abroad, mutual love was exhibited between people and people, the members of Christ's body were united in complete harmony.

Then was fulfilled the prophetic utterance which mystically foretold what was to take place: "Bone to bone and joint to joint," and whatever was truly announced in enigmatic expressions in the inspired passage.

And there was one energy of the Divine Spirit pervading all the members, and one soul in all, and the same eagerness of faith, and one hymn from all in praise of the Deity.

So when the prophet spoke what he had been commanded, at once a commotion arose; and the bones were fitted into their framework, bound with sinews, full of flesh, covered with hide; and there lay human bodies that did not have spirit.

If you are skeptical that ashes can be reassembled into bodies and souls restored to their vessels, Ezekiel will be your witness, for long ago the whole process of resurrection was revealed to him by the Lord. In his pages you will behold the dusty remains of people of old come to life over the entire region, bones scattered far and wide over the broad plain spontaneously hastening to fuse together when bidden, sprouting sinews from the innermost marrow and then drawing the skin over the flesh that had grown on them. Then the limbs are perfectly ordered more quickly than words can tell, and from the ancient dust stand forth people made new.

The proclamation, he says is made by me, by divine command. The bodies that were bound together came back to life, and they experienced a resurrection, and the multitude of those who rose again was not small.

And again, the blessed Ezekiel says: And it was as I prophesied, and behold a shaking and the bones came together, bone to his bone, each to its own joint: and when I beheld, lo, the sinews came up upon them and the flesh grew and rose up on them and the skin covered them above. And later he teaches how the spirits came back when they were bidden.
An Exact Exposition of the Orthodox Faith, Book 4, Chapter 27

Of course I could do nothing—I could not last out one hour—without continual conscious recourse to what I called Spirit. But the fine, philosophical distinction between this and what ordinary people call "prayer to God" breaks down as soon as you start doing it in earnest. Idealism can be talked, and even felt; it cannot be lived. It became patently absurd to go on thinking of "Spirit" as either ignorant of, or passive to, my approaches. Even if my own philosophy were true, how could the initiative lie on my side? My own analogy, as I now first perceived, suggested the opposite: if Shakespeare and Hamlet could ever meet, it must be Shakespeare's doing. Hamlet could initiate nothing. Perhaps, even now, my Absolute Spirit still differed in some way from the God of religion. The real issue was not, or not yet, there. The real terror was that if you seriously believed in even such a "God" or "Spirit" as I admitted, a wholly new situation developed. As the dry bones shook and came together in that dreadful valley of Ezekiel's, so now a philosophical theorem, cerebrally entertained, began to stir and heave and throw off its gravecloths, and stood upright and became a living presence. I was to be allowed to play at philosophy no longer.

Therefore the prophet prophesies to the spirit, and says: Thus says the Lord God: Come from the four winds, O spirit — namely from the four quarters of the world, so that, just as in the first creation of man: God breathed into his face and he was made into a living soul, so also the second creation, that is, the resurrection of the dead, may be given life by the breathing of the spirit —, and the spirit entered the human bodies, and at once they lived and stood upon their feet — whence also the resurrection of the dead is called a 'congregation', or church, 'large' and, as it is in the Hebrew, 'a great army'; and at that time is fulfilled: Send forth your spirit and they shall be created, and you shall renew the face of the earth —.
He will contemplate truly admirable souls that have been brought back from the grave to reanimate completely consumed bodies.

But what follows: And he said to me: Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel, seems to raise a question, in that it is said not of the general resurrection but properly of the resurrection of the house of Israel, which says: 'Our bones have dried up and our hope has perished, and we are cut off from our land' or 'we have utterly despaired'; and as they say these things, Ezekiel is compelled to prophesy a third time and to say to the dry bones: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will open your tombs, and here it is asked, if he opens tombs, how he said above: And they were very many upon the face of the plain, and exceedingly dry. And I will lead, he says, you out of your graves, my people — according to what is written in the Gospel: The hour comes when those who are in the graves shall hear the voice of the Son of God; and those who have done good shall come forth to the resurrection of life, and again: Those who hear shall live —. And if, as some think, the divine word speaks of the general resurrection, what need was there to say specifically: And I will bring you into the land of Israel, when throughout the whole world the dead must rise from those places in which they were buried? And when, he says, I have led you out of your tombs and have put my spirit in you and you have lived, then: 'I will make you rest upon your own soil, so that, after you have rested in the land of Israel, you may then know that I am the Lord, who have fulfilled my promises in deed'. Those, then, who understand these words of the general resurrection refer what seems to raise a question: These bones are the whole house of Israel, to the resurrection of the saints — of which the apostle John also speaks in the Revelation: Blessed and holy is he who has part in the first resurrection; over him the second death has no power —, namely that the resurrection of the saints is one thing, that of sinners another — whence also it is said in the first psalm: The ungodly shall not rise again in judgment, nor sinners in the council of the righteous —; and the land of Israel, which the Lord promises to those who rise again, they affirm to be that of which it is written: Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the land, and: I will please the Lord in the region of the living. These things are said by those who hold that Ezekiel wrote, as we have said, of the general resurrection.
It is a prerogative of God to raise the dead.

We notice here how the operations of the Spirit of life are again resumed; we know in what way the dead are raised from the opening tombs. And is it in truth a matter of wonder that the sepulchers of the dead are opened at the bidding of the Lord, when the whole earth from its utmost limits is shaken by one thunderclap, the sea overflows its bounds and again checks the course of its waves?

But if the Jews and judaizing Christians wish to refer these things to the reign of a thousand years, they will be compelled by necessity to accept that all who have been saved will dwell in the land of Israel, that Jerusalem is to be built, the temple to be erected, all the ceremonies of the law to be practiced, the sabbath to be observed, the injury of circumcision to be received, that there is to be eating and drinking, and that an abundance of riches is to be esteemed as the highest blessedness and all wealth, when the Apostle says: Food for the belly and the belly for foods: but God will destroy both it and them; but just as, in the type of the resurrection, the preceding prophetic word showed the restoration of the Jewish people, not carnal but spiritual, so also this prophecy pertains not at all to the happiness of the flesh but to that of the soul, and to the faith of Christ, by which we are cleansed in baptism, whose kingdom is for ever, so that we may not await as things to come what has already been accomplished and what we know is accomplished daily.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: And you, son of man, take for yourself one stick and write upon it: Of Judah and of the sons of Israel his companions. And take another stick and write upon it: Of Joseph — the stick of Ephraim — and of the house of Israel and of his companions. And join them one to the other for yourself into one stick; and they shall be in union in your hand. And when the sons of your people say to you, speaking: Will you not show us what you mean by these things? you shall speak to them: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will take the stick of Joseph — which is in the hand of Ephraim — and the tribes of Israel which are joined to him, and I will put them together with the stick of Judah and make them one stick, and they shall be one in his hand. And the sticks on which you have written shall be in your hand before their eyes, and you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will take the sons of Israel from the midst of the nations to which they have gone, and I will gather them from every side, and I will bring them to their own soil, and I will make them one nation in the land on the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be ruling over all, and they shall no longer be two nations, nor shall they be divided any more into two kingdoms. Nor shall they be defiled any more with their idols and abominations and with all their iniquities, and I will save them out of all their dwelling places in which they sinned, and I will cleanse them, and they shall be my people, and I will be their God. And my servant David shall be king over them, and there shall be one shepherd of them all; they shall walk in my judgments, and they shall keep my commandments and do them. And they shall dwell upon the land which I gave to my servant Jacob, in which your fathers dwelt; and they shall dwell upon it, they and their sons and their sons' sons for ever, and David my servant shall be their prince for ever. And I will strike with them a covenant of peace, it shall be an everlasting pact for them, and I will establish them and multiply them; and I will put my sanctification in the midst of them for ever, and my tabernacle shall be among them; and the nations shall know that I am the Lord, the sanctifier of Israel, when my sanctification shall be in the midst of them for ever. (LXX: "And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: And you, son of man, take to yourself one rod and write upon it: Judah and the sons of Israel who are added to him. And you shall take to yourself a second rod and you shall inscribe it: Joseph — the rod of Ephraim — and all the sons of Israel who are added to him. And you shall join them to each other for yourself into one rod, so as to couple them; and they shall be in your hand. And it shall be, when the sons of Israel say to you, speaking: Will you not show us what these things are to you? you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I will take into the tribe of Joseph — through the hand of Ephraim — the tribes of Israel which are joined to him, and I will put them all upon the tribe of Judah and they shall be into one rod, and they shall be one in the hand of Judah. And the rods which you inscribed shall be thus, in your hand in their presence, and you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I will take the whole house of Israel from the midst of the nations into which they have entered, and I will gather them from all who are round about it, and I will bring them into the land of Israel, and I will make them into one nation in my land on the mountains of Israel; and one prince shall be over all these as king, and they shall no longer be into two nations, nor shall they be divided any more into two kingdoms. And let them no longer be defiled with their idols and with their stumbling blocks and with all their impieties, and I will rescue them from all their iniquities in which they sinned, and I will cleanse them, and they shall be to me for a people: I will be to them for God. And my servant David shall be prince in their midst, and there shall be one shepherd of all these, for they shall walk in my precepts and keep my judgments and do them. And they shall dwell in their own land which I gave to my servant Jacob, where their fathers dwelt; and they shall dwell in it, they and their sons and their sons' sons for ever, and David my servant shall be their prince for ever. And I will appoint for them a testament of peace, it shall be an everlasting testament with them, and I will give them and multiply them; and I will set my holy things in their midst for ever, and my tabernacle shall be among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people; and the nations shall know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them, when my holy things shall be in their midst for ever.") The history of the Kings relates that under Rehoboam the son of Solomon the twelve tribes were divided, and that two, that is, Judah and Benjamin, with the Levites and priests, followed Rehoboam, who reigned in Jerusalem: and his kingdom was called Judah; but that the other ten tribes — who said: We have no part in David, nor inheritance in the son of Jesse — submitted their necks to Jeroboam the son of Nebat, of the tribe of Ephraim, who was the son of Joseph, and served him: and that they were called, from the greater part of the people, by the ancient name Israel; and that for a long time the kingdom of Judah and Israel waged conflicts against each other and obeyed their own kings, and that first the ten tribes were taken captive by the Assyrians, and, after some time, those which were called Judah were led captive by the Chaldeans into Babylon; and that the tribe of Judah was restored to its ancient land after seventy years, but the ten tribes, which were called Israel, serve as captives to this day in the mountains and cities of the Medes. The present prophecy, therefore, promises these things from the mouth of the Lord: that both realms are to be joined together, that is, the kingdom of Judah and the kingdom of Israel, and that the rod of Ephraim, who was begotten of the stock of Joseph, is to be taken up with the remaining tribes which are associated with him, and joined to the rod of Judah, so that they are no longer called Judah and Israel but are called by one name, Judah, and, under the figure of the prophet, who goes before as a type of the Lord Savior, are held not by two hands but by the one hand of Christ.
